claim.exact_statement: For every Boolean seed g on m>=1 uniform core coordinates, every physical vertex x0, and r>=1 dummy padding coordinates, let F_r differ from g only at (x0,all +), let d=2^(1-m-r), and let I_core=sum of the core-coordinate influences of F_r. For every physical tree that queries only padding coordinates along the unique edited branch and stops every clean branch, the total expected entropy drop Q_pad satisfies Q_pad<=4 I_queried+(1+6/ln(2)) I_core. The core reserve is allocated once across the whole tree. If every leaf satisfies U<=b I, b>=0, where U=sum_nonempty hat f(S)^2(max{|T|:hat f(T)!=0,T contains S}-|S|), then H(F_r)<=(3+2b+6/ln(2)) I(F_r); a sufficient admission is U(g)<=b I(g) and U(F_0)<=b I(F_0). For fixed finite g and r>=2, with L the number of its nonzero Fourier coefficients and p=2^(-m-r), the padding-node drop Delta_r obeys |Delta_r/(2p)-4|<=4 L p (|m+r-3|+m+3/(2ln(2))), hence the ratio tends to 4. The point-defect padding nodes satisfy 0<=Delta<=5 Inf at every dimension. Consequently dictator one-point surgery and Maj3 tensor point defects have explicit U<=I stopping trees paid at node rate 5, with full terminal entropy retained. There is no uniform padding-node rate for arbitrary varying seeds: quadratic bent seeds of even dimension m at fixed r>=2 have Delta_r/(2p)=4+2^(1-r)(m+2r-6+3/ln(2))+O(2^(-r)*2^(1-m/2-r)). These are a padding-access theorem and its scope guards, not universal admission of arbitrary Boolean core leaves.
